The system uses a Claude-based LLM for extraction but includes a deterministic rule-based path that works without a network connection.

Missing data fields are labeled as 'NA' in the final report to prevent generation failures.

The application uses ReportLab and matplotlib to render PDF reports and charts, requiring at least two charts to be populated.

Standardized financial reports are achievable by decoupling data extraction from document rendering.

claims.text: The web application converts financial documents in PDF, CSV, or TXT formats into auto-filled PDF research reports.
The report layout is designed to mirror the structure of Geojit-style equity research notes.
The application provides a quick start process that takes less than two minutes to set up.
The extraction process offers two modes: a Claude-based LLM path that requires an API key, and a deterministic rule-based path that functions without a network connection.
The system is designed to degrade gracefully to deterministic parsing if the LLM call encounters an error.
The application uses ReportLab and matplotlib to render PDF reports and charts respectively.
The system requires at least two charts, specifically a revenue trend and a margin trend, to be populated in the report.
Fields that cannot be located during the extraction process are labeled as 'NA' in the final report.
The tech stack includes Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Jinja2, and pdfplumber.
The application uses a FastAPI-based structure with a dedicated configuration file for managing visual elements like fonts, colors, and the rating ladder.
Data extraction is handled by an orchestrator that utilizes LLMs with a deterministic fallback mechanism.
To achieve an exact visual match with a specific Geojit PDF, users can modify the geometry and section spacing within the PDF builder file.
The data model and extraction logic remain independent of the document's visual styling.
This project is a reconstructed template for educational purposes and holds no official affiliation with Geojit Financial Services Ltd.
Reports produced by this tool do not constitute investment advice.
